title: Most parsing errors from loading a resource returns exactly the same line instead of line closer to the parsing error and sometimes are not helpful.
body:
### Tested versions

- v4.8.dev.custom_build [00932449c]
- v4.7.1.stable.custom_build [a13da4feb]

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable (a13da4feb) - 'Gentoo' '2.18' on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 (nvidia; 595.84) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 15.54 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

If you have a parsing error of any sort, an error appears in the output:
```
  ERROR: scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp:41 - res://scene_loaded.tscn:7 - Parse Error: .
  ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://scene_loaded.tscn.
  ERROR: scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp:41 - res://scene_loaded.tscn:7 - Parse Error: .
  ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://scene_loaded.tscn.
```
`scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp:41` is this line:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3000096f9aa6f46db98d3a6d2a9442d58cab96ac/scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp#L41

Which is just the printer, the actual source of the error cannot be found unless you do something of the sort:
* Open Godot with a debugger.
* Add a breakpoint in line `scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp:41`
* Open the problematic file
* Follow the call stack to where the printer was called.
* In this case, it came from around here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3000096f9aa6f46db98d3a6d2a9442d58cab96ac/scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp#L648-L651

If you are lucky and the error is obvious, you can just search the codebase for the error. But you also need to be luck that the same error does not repeat elsewhere in the code base.

As a side note, that error above came from the MRP of the issue #83187, it's not an actual parsing error, the returned error is `ERR_BUSY`, instead of `ERR_FILE_CORRUPT` that tends to be returned when the file is not fully correct. But it is still being treated as such.

### Steps to reproduce

* Save scene as tscn (for example):
  ```toml
  [gd_scene format=3 uid="uid://bnx247jqbp4k0"]

  [node name="Node" type="Node" unique_id=1338681539]
  ```
* Add a `.` after `[node`
  ```toml
  [gd_scene format=3 uid="uid://bnx247jqbp4k0"]

  [node. name="Node" type="Node" unique_id=1338681539]
  ```
* Open the scene file in the editor, the error will be:
  ```
   ERROR: scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp:41 - res://invalid.tscn:3 - Parse Error: Unexpected end of file.
   ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://invalid.tscn.
   ERROR: editor/editor_node.cpp:1623 - Failed to load scene: res://invalid.tscn
  ```
  The actual error comes from around:
  https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3000096f9aa6f46db98d3a6d2a9442d58cab96ac/scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp#L1193-L1201
  And there's no end of file, there's just a stray dot.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

you may use the MRP of  and follow their instructions #83187

Or download this one that have just a corrupt scene file.

[corrupt-file-example.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31157819/corrupt-file-example.zip)
